- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes, then sharply drop — suggesting overshoot and failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly after a spike, indicating lag or failure to adjust to downward momentum.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices — model fails to reflect mean reversion or downward pressure.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts remain elevated even when true prices are falling or consolidating.
- When true prices drop sharply after a spike, model fails to anticipate the drop, often forecasting a plateau or slight recovery instead.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, suggesting it doesn’t capture the “tail risk” or end-of-period correction.
- Forecasts are often too optimistic in the first 10 days, then too pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggesting asymmetric bias or poor horizon calibration.
